name: cortexcn
description: Build UI with Cortexcn, the React and Tailwind CSS registry at ui.cortexcn.dev. Use when the user mentions Cortexcn or @cortexcn, asks for a component, page block, or chart in a project that uses Cortexcn, or wants to find, install, compose, or theme Cortexcn items.
---

# Cortexcn

Cortexcn is a registry of React components, page blocks, and charts built with Tailwind CSS. Items install with the shadcn CLI, which copies the source into the project, so the code belongs to the project and there is no runtime package to update.

- Site and docs: https://ui.cortexcn.dev
- Registry index: https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/registry.json
- One item: `https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/<name>.json`
- Any docs page as markdown: add `.md` to its URL, for example https://ui.cortexcn.dev/docs/components/lanyard-3d.md
- Every docs page in one file: https://ui.cortexcn.dev/llms-full.txt

## Find the right item

If the `cortexcn` MCP server is connected, use it:

1. `search_items` with what the user needs, such as "pricing hero" or "line chart with tooltip". Pass `kind` (`component`, `block`, `chart`) to narrow it.
2. `get_item` on the best match. It returns the install command, the files and dependencies, and the docs with usage and props.
3. `get_design_guide` before writing new UI around it.

Without the MCP server, read the registry index above, then the item's docs page as markdown.

Kinds of items:

- **Components**: building blocks such as buttons, dialogs, and menus, plus Cortexcn originals such as Lanyard 3D, Gooey Nav, and Sphere Menu.
- **Blocks**: whole page sections such as heroes, feature grids, loaders, stat cards, and AI assistant pieces. Their props have defaults filled with example content, so they render as soon as they are added.
- **Charts**: composable charts. A chart is assembled from parts (the chart, grid, axes, tooltip, legend), so read its docs page for the parts it takes.

## Install

The project needs shadcn set up. If there is no `components.json` in the project root, run `npx shadcn@latest init` first.

Install by URL, which needs no further setup:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/lanyard-3d.json
```

Several items at once:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/hero-studio-01.json https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/area-chart.json
```

To install by name, add the registry to `components.json` once:

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@cortexcn": "https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Then `npx shadcn@latest add @cortexcn/lanyard-3d`. Use the package manager the project already uses (`pnpm dlx`, `npx`, or `bunx --bun`).

The CLI installs the item's npm dependencies and the other registry items it needs. Read the files it reports and import from the paths it wrote them to, which follow the aliases in `components.json` (usually `@/components/<name>`).

## Use it well

- Read the props from the docs. Never guess a prop or an item name.
- The installed files are the project's own code. Edit them when the design needs it, and keep their `data-slot` attributes, which other styles and tests rely on.
- Interactive items are client components (`"use client"`). In the Next.js App Router, keep them in client files or pass them server-rendered children.
- Compose before you create: check whether a Cortexcn item already does the job before writing a new one.
- Blocks are starting points. Replace the example copy, links, and images with the user's own through props, or edit the block's file.

## Look and feel

Cortexcn has a square, quiet look. Follow the project's `DESIGN.md` if it has one (install it with `npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/design-md.json`, or read it from `get_design_guide`). In short:

- Colors come from theme tokens only: `bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `bg-muted`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-primary`, `text-primary-foreground`, `ring-ring`, and `--chart-1` to `--chart-5` for data. No hard-coded hex values.
- Corners come from the radius scale (`rounded-md`, `rounded-lg`), which Cortexcn sets to square with `--radius: 0`. Do not hard-code a radius such as `rounded-[12px]`.
- Every interactive element keeps a visible focus ring (`focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50`).
- Light and dark mode both work from the same tokens; dark mode is the `.dark` class.
- Motion is short (100 to 300 ms), eases out, and stops when the user prefers reduced motion.

## Check before you finish

- The install command ran without errors and the imports resolve.
- No hard-coded colors or radii were added.
- It works in light and dark mode, with the keyboard, and with reduced motion.

name: cortexcn-design
description: Apply the Cortexcn design system. Use before creating, restyling, or reviewing any UI in a project that has a DESIGN.md or uses Cortexcn, so colors, corners, type, spacing, and motion follow the system; and when theme tokens change, to update DESIGN.md.
---

# Cortexcn design

`DESIGN.md` at the project root is the source of truth for how the interface looks. Read it before you write UI, and follow it over your own taste.

If the project has no `DESIGN.md`, add the Cortexcn one:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.cortexcn.dev/r/design-md.json
```

Or read it from the `cortexcn` MCP server with `get_design_guide`.

## Workflow

1. Read `DESIGN.md`, then the theme CSS it points to (usually `app/globals.css`), so you know the real token names in this project.
2. Before adding anything new, look for a Cortexcn item that already does it (the `cortexcn` skill explains how to search and install).
3. Build with tokens and the scales in `DESIGN.md`: colors, radius, spacing, type, shadows, and motion.
4. Check the result against the list below, in light and dark mode.

## Rules

- **Color**: only theme tokens, as Tailwind classes such as `bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `bg-card`, `bg-muted`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-primary`, `text-primary-foreground`, `bg-destructive`, and `ring-ring`. Data uses `--chart-1` to `--chart-5`. Tints use opacity on a token (`bg-primary/10`), never a new hex value.
- **Corners**: square. The radius scale (`rounded-sm` to `rounded-4xl`) is derived from `--radius`, which is `0`. Use the scale classes so a theme can change it in one place; never hard-code a radius.
- **Borders and depth**: one-pixel `border-border` lines separate surfaces. Shadows are rare and soft (`shadow-xs`, `shadow-sm`); prefer a border or a `bg-muted` panel.
- **Type**: the project's sans font for interface text, `font-medium` for labels and buttons, `text-sm` as the default control size, `text-muted-foreground` for secondary text. Headings use tight tracking (`tracking-tight`) and `text-balance`.
- **Spacing**: Tailwind's 4 px scale. Controls are `h-9` by default (`h-8` small, `h-10` large); gaps inside controls are `gap-1.5`.
- **Focus**: every interactive element shows `focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50`. Never remove the outline without a replacement.
- **Motion**: 100 to 300 ms, easing out, on `transform` and `opacity` where possible. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and stop or shorten animation for it.
- **Dark mode**: the `.dark` class swaps the tokens. Do not write separate dark colors unless `DESIGN.md` lists them.
- **Components**: keep `data-slot` attributes, compose with `cn()`, and add variants with `class-variance-authority` the way existing components do.

## Before you finish

- No hex, rgb, or oklch values in components; no hard-coded radius.
- Light and dark mode both read well, with enough contrast for text.
- Keyboard focus is visible on every control.
- Reduced motion turns off or shortens every animation.

## When the tokens change

If the theme CSS changes (new colors, radius, or fonts), update the matching tables in `DESIGN.md` in the same change, so the next agent reads the truth.

# Cortexcn

## Overview

Cortexcn is a set of React components, page blocks, and charts built with Tailwind CSS and shadcn conventions. The look is square and quiet: neutral surfaces, one-pixel borders, no rounded corners, and color used for meaning rather than decoration. Everything is driven by CSS custom properties, so the same components work in light and dark mode and follow a project's own theme.

This file is generated from `cortexcn-tokens.css`. The front matter holds the tokens; the sections below explain how to use them. When a request conflicts with these rules, follow the rules and say so.

## Colors

Use colors only through the theme tokens, as Tailwind classes: `bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `bg-card`, `bg-muted`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-primary`, `text-primary-foreground`, `bg-destructive`, `ring-ring`, and `fill-chart-1` to `fill-chart-5` for data. Tints are opacity on a token (`bg-primary/10`, `border-border/60`), never a new color.

Dark mode is the `.dark` class on an ancestor, usually `<html>`. It swaps every token at once, so components never need their own dark colors. The `-dark` keys in the front matter are the values under `.dark`.

## Typography

Interface text uses the project's sans font. Cortexcn's own site sets Geist; any neutral sans works.

- Default control and body size in components is `text-sm` (14px). Long-form text is `text-base` (16px).
- Labels, buttons, and table headers are `font-medium`. Headings are `font-semibold` with `tracking-tight` and `text-balance`.
- Secondary text is `text-muted-foreground`, not a lighter weight.
- Numbers that line up or change, such as stats, prices, and tables, use `tabular-nums`.
- Code and keyboard keys use the mono font at `text-xs` or `text-sm`.

## Layout

Spacing follows Tailwind's 4px scale. Inside controls the gap is `gap-1.5` (6px); between related items `gap-2` to `gap-4`; between sections `gap-12` to `gap-24`.

- Controls are `h-9` (36px) by default, `h-8` small, `h-10` large, with `px-2.5` padding.
- Cards and panels use `p-6` (24px), or `p-4` when dense.
- Page content sits in a centered container with `px-4` on phones and `px-6` or more on wider screens.
- Lay out with flex and grid gaps, not margins between siblings.

## Elevation & Depth

Depth comes from borders and surface color first. A card is `bg-card` with `border-border` on a `bg-background` page. Shadows are rare and soft (`shadow-xs` on outline buttons, `shadow-sm` on floating elements), and in dark mode the shadow token is transparent, so borders carry the separation.

## Shapes

Corners are square. `--radius` is `0`, and every `rounded-*` utility (`rounded-sm` to `rounded-4xl`) is derived from it, so components written with the radius scale come out square. Use the scale classes, never a hard-coded radius such as `rounded-[12px]`, so a theme can change the radius in one place. `rounded-full` stays round and is for avatars, status dots, and switches.

## Components

- Build from the existing Cortexcn and shadcn components before writing new ones. Keep their `data-slot` attributes; styles and tests rely on them.
- Compose classes with `cn()` and add variants with `class-variance-authority`, the way `Button` does.
- Buttons: `default` (primary), `outline`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `destructive` (a tinted fill, not solid red), and `link`. One primary action per view.
- Inputs: a one-pixel `border-input`, transparent fill, and a visible focus ring.
- Focus: every interactive element shows `focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50`. Never remove the outline without that replacement.
- Motion: 100 to 300 ms, easing out, on `transform` and `opacity` where possible. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by turning motion off or shortening it.
- Icons are 16px (`size-4`) in controls and inherit `currentColor`.

## Do's and Don'ts

Do:

- Use the token classes for every color and the radius scale for every corner.
- Check light and dark mode, keyboard focus, and reduced motion before you finish.
- Keep one primary action per view and let the rest be `outline` or `ghost`.
- Separate surfaces with `border-border` and `bg-card` before reaching for a shadow.

Don't:

- Don't write hex, rgb, or oklch values in components, or add per-component dark colors.
- Don't round corners by hand or mix rounded and square elements.
- Don't use color alone to carry meaning; pair it with text or an icon.
- Don't animate layout properties such as width and height when a transform does the job.
